cert.name: Databricks Certified Data Engineer Associate
cert.guide: Exam published 4 May 2026, exam guide updated 6 Aug 2026
cert.disclaimer: Independent practice written by Datakul from the public exam guide. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Databricks, and not real exam questions.

questions.q: What gives a Delta Lake table ACID transactions on top of files in cloud storage?
opts: A transaction log of ordered commits stored next to the data files
A separate relational database that holds every row
Locking each Parquet file while it is being read
Writing every table as a single large file
questions.why: Delta Lake records every change as a commit in the _delta_log folder. Readers use the log to see a consistent snapshot and writers add new commits, so changes are atomic and isolated even though the data itself is ordinary Parquet files.

questions.q: A team needs compute for a nightly scheduled pipeline and wants the lowest cost with no idle time. Which choice fits best?
opts: An all-purpose cluster left running all day
Job compute (or serverless jobs compute) that starts for the run and stops when it finishes
A SQL warehouse sized extra large
The driver node of a teammate's interactive cluster
questions.why: Job compute exists only for the run and is billed at a lower rate than all-purpose compute, which is meant for interactive work. Serverless jobs compute removes start-up management too. Leaving an all-purpose cluster running wastes money while idle.

questions.q: Analysts run SQL dashboards all day with many concurrent users. Which compute is designed for this?
opts: A SQL warehouse
Single-node job compute
A notebook's local Python process
An all-purpose cluster with one worker
questions.why: SQL warehouses are built for SQL and BI workloads: they scale for concurrent queries, and serverless warehouses start in seconds. Job and all-purpose clusters can run SQL but are not designed for many concurrent BI users.

questions.q: In Unity Catalog, what is the order of the three-level namespace used to name a table?
opts: schema.catalog.table
catalog.schema.table
metastore.table.column
workspace.catalog.table
questions.why: Tables are addressed as catalog.schema.table, for example main.sales.orders. The metastore sits above catalogs, and the same three-level name works in every workspace attached to that metastore.

questions.q: A COPY INTO command that loaded 500 files yesterday runs again today. Twenty new files have arrived in the same folder. What happens?
opts: All 520 files are loaded again, creating duplicates
Only the 20 new files are loaded, because COPY INTO skips files it has already loaded
The command fails because the target table is not empty
It loads only files modified in the last hour
questions.why: COPY INTO keeps track of the files it has loaded into a table and skips them on later runs, so rerunning it is safe and loads only new files. That idempotency is why it suits scheduled incremental loads of a few thousand files.

questions.q: Millions of small JSON files land in cloud storage every day and must be loaded incrementally with minimal setup. Which option is the best fit?
opts: Auto Loader (the cloudFiles source)
A daily full read of the folder with spark.read.json
COPY INTO with a list of every file name
Manually uploading files through the UI
questions.why: Auto Loader is designed for continuous or very high volumes of files. It tracks processed files in a checkpoint and can use file notifications instead of listing huge folders. Rereading the whole folder every day duplicates work and data.

questions.q: An Auto Loader stream reads JSON with schema evolution left at its default. A new field appears in incoming files. What happens by default?
opts: The new field is silently dropped forever
The stream stops, updates the stored schema with the new column, and picks it up when restarted
Every record with the new field is deleted
The table is recreated from scratch
questions.why: The default mode, addNewColumns, adds the new column to the schema stored at the schema location and stops the stream so the change is noticed. When it restarts, records include the new column. Jobs are usually set to retry so this happens automatically.

questions.q: With Auto Loader, where do values go that don't match the expected schema, such as a string in an integer column, when rescue is enabled?
opts: They are cast to NULL with no trace
Into the _rescued_data column, so nothing is lost
Into a separate error table that must be created first
The whole file is skipped
questions.why: The rescued data column, _rescued_data by default, keeps values that couldn't be parsed into the schema as JSON, along with the source file path. You can inspect and reprocess them later instead of losing data.

questions.q: You want Auto Loader to process all files available now and then stop, so it can run as a scheduled batch job. Which trigger do you use?
opts: trigger(availableNow=True)
trigger(processingTime='0 seconds')
trigger(continuous='1 second')
No trigger, and kill the job after an hour
questions.why: availableNow processes every file that has arrived since the last run, in as many batches as needed, then stops. It gives incremental, exactly-once file processing on a schedule without paying for an always-on stream.

questions.q: When should Auto Loader use file notification mode instead of directory listing mode?
opts: When the input folder is small and rarely changes
When the folder receives very large numbers of files and listing it on every run becomes slow and costly
Only when the files are CSV
Never: directory listing is always faster
questions.why: Directory listing works well for modest folders but has to list storage to find new files. File notification mode (and the newer file events, which the docs prefer) reads storage events, so it scales to huge numbers of files without repeated listing.

questions.q: A company wants to ingest data from Salesforce and SQL Server into Unity Catalog tables with Databricks managing the connection, incremental reads and schema changes. What should they consider first?
opts: Lakeflow Connect managed connectors
Writing a custom REST client for each source
Exporting CSV files by hand every morning
Auto Loader pointed at the source databases
questions.why: Lakeflow Connect provides managed connectors for common SaaS applications and databases, handling authentication, incremental ingestion and schema evolution. Auto Loader reads files in cloud storage, not databases or SaaS APIs.

questions.q: A source system offers only a REST API with no Databricks connector. What is a sensible way to land its data?
opts: Call the API from a notebook, write the results to a bronze Delta table, and schedule it as a Lakeflow Jobs task
Ask analysts to copy and paste results into a spreadsheet
Point Auto Loader at the API URL
Use COPY INTO with the API URL as the source
questions.why: When no connector exists, a notebook using a REST or JDBC client can fetch data and write it to a Delta table, orchestrated by Lakeflow Jobs for scheduling and retries. Auto Loader and COPY INTO read files from storage, not APIs. The docs also describe a decoupled pattern: the notebook writes raw JSON to a volume and Auto Loader loads it.

more.t: Ingest data from an API in pipelines

questions.q: A JSON column holds an array of line items per order. You need one row per line item in a silver table. Which function do you use?
opts: explode
flatten_all
split
pivot
questions.why: explode turns each element of an array into its own row, repeating the other columns. split breaks a string into an array, and pivot turns row values into columns.
questions.code:
SELECT order_id, item.sku, item.qty
FROM (
  SELECT order_id, explode(line_items) AS item
  FROM main.bronze.orders
)

questions.q: Which statements about loading files into Unity Catalog are true? (Choose two.)
opts: Volumes give governed access to files in cloud storage through Unity Catalog
COPY INTO can load files from a volume into a table
Files in a volume cannot be read by Spark
Auto Loader can only read files uploaded through the UI
questions.why: Volumes are Unity Catalog objects for files, governed with the same permissions as tables, and both COPY INTO and Auto Loader can read from volume paths such as /Volumes/catalog/schema/volume/. Spark reads volume files like any other path.

questions.q: COPY INTO loaded a folder yesterday. Today one of yesterday's files was corrected in place and 20 new files arrived. Without any options, what does COPY INTO load?
opts: Only the 20 new files; the corrected file is skipped because it was already loaded
All files in the folder again
The 20 new files and the corrected file
Nothing, because the folder has already been loaded
questions.why: COPY INTO is idempotent: it skips files it has already loaded, even when the file was changed afterwards. To reload on purpose, set the force copy option and name the files with FILES or PATTERN, otherwise every matching file is loaded again.

questions.q: An Auto Loader stream has no schema supplied and the default schema evolution mode. Today's files contain a new field. What happens?
opts: The stream stops once, saves the new column to the schema location, and uses it after a restart
The new field is silently ignored forever
All existing rows are rewritten with the new column immediately
The stream keeps running and the field is dropped
questions.why: The default with no schema is addNewColumns: the stream fails with an unknown-field error after updating the stored schema, and the restart picks the new column up. Run it under a job with retries. Use rescue to never stop, or failOnNewColumns to demand attention.

more.t: Auto Loader schema inference and evolution

questions.q: Auto Loader is given amount as a DOUBLE, but a record contains the text "N/A". Where does the value go?
opts: Into the _rescued_data column, with the source file path
The stream fails and nothing more loads
It is turned into 0.0
It is written to a hidden error table you must create
questions.why: Values that do not match the schema are kept in the rescued data column as JSON with the file path, so nothing is lost and the stream keeps running. Query it with a colon path where _rescued_data IS NOT NULL.

more.t: Auto Loader schema inference and evolution

questions.q: Which statements about Lakeflow Connect managed database connectors are true? (Choose two.)
opts: The ingestion gateway runs continuously on classic compute and is billed while it runs
The ingestion pipeline can run on a schedule on serverless compute
Both the gateway and the pipeline must run on a single-user all-purpose cluster
They read the source tables by running a full copy on every update
questions.why: A managed database connector has a gateway that stays on to capture changes and a pipeline that applies them on a schedule, so the gateway is the cost to watch. It reads change logs rather than copying whole tables each time.

questions.q: Clickstream JSON has stable event_id and ts fields and a properties object whose keys change weekly. How should it be loaded for fast filtering on event_id and ts?
opts: Type event_id and ts as columns and keep properties as a VARIANT column
Store the whole record as one VARIANT column and partition by a field inside it
Store everything as one string and parse it on every query
Drop properties, since it changes
questions.why: Typed columns filter faster, and VARIANT cannot be used as a partition or clustering key. Keeping only the changing part as VARIANT stays flexible. Declare it through cloudFiles.schemaHints.

questions.q: In PySpark, df1.union(df2) is called on two DataFrames with the same columns in a different order. What happens?
opts: Columns are matched by name automatically
Columns are matched by position, so values can end up in the wrong columns; use unionByName instead
Duplicates are removed like SQL UNION
It always raises an error
questions.why: DataFrame.union matches columns by position and keeps duplicates, like SQL UNION ALL. If column order differs, values land in the wrong columns. unionByName matches by column name.

questions.q: What is the difference between UNION and UNION ALL in Spark SQL?
opts: UNION removes duplicate rows; UNION ALL keeps every row and is cheaper
UNION ALL removes duplicates; UNION keeps them
They are identical
UNION ALL only works on streaming tables
questions.why: UNION de-duplicates the combined result, which needs a shuffle. UNION ALL simply appends, so it is faster. Use UNION ALL unless you really need duplicates removed.

questions.q: A 5 TB orders table is joined to a 20 MB country lookup table. How can you avoid shuffling the large table?
opts: Broadcast the small table, for example with a broadcast hint
Repartition the orders table to 10,000 partitions
Convert the lookup table to CSV
Use a cross join
questions.why: A broadcast join sends the small table to every executor, so each partition of the large table joins locally with no shuffle. Spark does this automatically below spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold, and a hint forces it.
questions.code:
SELECT /*+ BROADCAST(c) */ o.*, c.country_name
FROM main.silver.orders o
JOIN main.ref.countries c ON o.country_code = c.code

questions.q: You need to keep one row per order_id from a bronze table where retries created duplicates. Which PySpark call does this?
opts: df.dropDuplicates(["order_id"])
df.distinct("order_id")
df.drop("order_id")
df.groupBy("order_id")
questions.why: dropDuplicates with a subset keeps one row for each value of the listed columns. distinct takes no column list and compares whole rows, and groupBy needs an aggregation. To choose which duplicate survives, use a window with row_number instead.

questions.q: A dashboard needs the number of distinct users per day over billions of events, and a small error is acceptable. Which function is fastest?
opts: approx_count_distinct
count(DISTINCT user_id) after collecting to the driver
collect_set then size
countDistinct on a cross join
questions.why: approx_count_distinct uses the HyperLogLog++ algorithm to estimate distinct counts with a small, configurable error, using far less memory and shuffle than an exact distinct count.

questions.q: When cleaning a bronze table, which PySpark call replaces NULL values in the quantity column with 0?
opts: df.fillna({"quantity": 0})
df.dropna("quantity")
df.replace(None, "quantity")
df.na.drop(0)
questions.why: fillna (also df.na.fill) replaces nulls with a value, here per column through a dictionary. dropna removes rows with nulls instead of filling them.

questions.q: A job joining two large tables writes 200 tiny output files and some tasks process far more data than others. Which setting controls how many partitions Spark uses after a shuffle?
opts: spark.sql.shuffle.partitions
spark.executor.cores
spark.driver.maxResultSize
spark.sql.files.maxRecordsPerFile
questions.why: spark.sql.shuffle.partitions sets the number of partitions after joins and aggregations; it defaults to 200. Adaptive query execution can coalesce partitions and split skewed ones at run time, but the setting is still the starting point to tune and re-measure.

questions.q: Which gold-layer object stores precomputed query results and is refreshed, incrementally where possible, when its sources change?
opts: A materialized view
A standard view
A temporary view
A volume
questions.why: A materialized view stores its results and is refreshed from its sources, incrementally when the query allows. A standard view stores no data and runs its query each time it is read.

questions.q: Which object is the best fit for append-only data that should be processed exactly once as it arrives, such as events from Auto Loader?
opts: A streaming table
A materialized view
A standard view
A temporary view
questions.why: Streaming tables process each new input row once, which suits append-only sources like files or event streams. Materialized views suit results that may need recomputing when sources change, such as aggregates and joins.

questions.q: In a Lakeflow Declarative Pipeline, a constraint is defined as below. What happens to rows where order_id is NULL?
opts: They are dropped from the target and counted in the pipeline's data quality metrics
The whole pipeline update fails
They are kept and nothing is recorded
They are moved to a quarantine table automatically
questions.why: ON VIOLATION DROP ROW removes failing rows and records how many were dropped. Without an ON VIOLATION clause, failing rows are kept and only counted, and ON VIOLATION FAIL UPDATE stops the update.

more.t: Manage data quality with pipeline expectations

questions.q: Which statements describe a medallion architecture? (Choose two.)
opts: Bronze holds raw data close to the source, kept for reprocessing
Silver holds cleaned, conformed data such as de-duplicated and typed records
Gold is where raw files first land
Each layer must live in a separate workspace
questions.why: Bronze keeps raw data so you can rebuild later, silver holds cleaned and conformed data, and gold holds business-level aggregates and models for BI and ML. Layers are usually schemas or catalogs, not separate workspaces.

questions.q: On serverless compute, a query runs cast(quantity AS INT) over a bronze column that contains values like "N/A". What happens, and what is the fix?
opts: The query fails because ANSI mode is on; use try_cast, which returns NULL for values that do not fit
Bad values silently become 0; use cast with a default
Bad values are moved to _rescued_data
The query succeeds and bad values stay as text
questions.why: Serverless runs with spark.sql.ansi.enabled set to true, so an invalid cast raises an error and stops the query. try_cast returns NULL instead, so you keep the row and can count the failures.

questions.q: Two DataFrames hold the same orders data, but the second has its columns in a different order and one extra column. Which call combines them correctly?
opts: df1.unionByName(df2, allowMissingColumns=True)
df1.union(df2)
df1.join(df2, how="cross")
df1.intersect(df2)
questions.why: union matches columns by position, so a different order puts values in the wrong columns. unionByName matches by name, and allowMissingColumns fills the missing column with NULL on the other side.

questions.q: Orders have an items array that is empty for cancelled orders. You need one row per item, but cancelled orders must still appear. Which function do you use?
opts: explode_outer
explode
flatten
split
questions.why: explode drops rows whose array is empty or NULL. explode_outer keeps them, with NULL in the new column.

questions.q: Bronze holds several versions of each order_id with an updated_at column. Which approach keeps exactly the latest version of each order?
opts: Keep rows where row_number() over PARTITION BY order_id ORDER BY updated_at DESC equals 1
df.dropDuplicates(["order_id"])
df.distinct()
GROUP BY order_id with max(updated_at) on its own
questions.why: dropDuplicates keeps one row per key but does not promise which one. row_number over a window ordered by updated_at picks the latest, and QUALIFY does it in one SQL statement. A plain GROUP BY with max returns the timestamp, not the rest of the row.

questions.q: Which statements about materialized views are true? (Choose two.)
opts: Incremental refresh needs serverless compute; on classic compute each refresh recomputes fully
A refresh can be scheduled in the definition, for example SCHEDULE EVERY 1 HOURS
A materialized view stores no data and runs its query on every read
A materialized view must be refreshed by hand with OPTIMIZE
questions.why: Materialized views store their result. When the query and sources allow, a refresh on serverless processes only the changes; otherwise it recomputes. The definition can carry a schedule or a trigger on source updates. OPTIMIZE and VACUUM are not supported because maintenance is automatic.

questions.q: In a pipeline, an expectation uses ON VIOLATION FAIL UPDATE and a bad row arrives. What happens?
opts: The update stops and the table write rolls back; no quality metrics are recorded for it
The bad row is dropped and counted
The bad row is kept and counted
The bad row is moved to a quarantine table automatically
questions.why: FAIL UPDATE stops the update, and someone must fix the cause before rerunning. Because the update failed, the Data quality tab has no metrics for it; read the error in the event log. DROP ROW removes and counts, and the default (warn) keeps and counts.

more.t: Manage data quality with pipeline expectations

questions.q: A notebook on a running classic cluster runs spark.conf.set("spark.executor.memory", "16g") to fix out-of-memory errors. Why doesn't it help?
opts: Executor memory is fixed when the cluster starts; change it in the compute configuration and restart
The value must be in megabytes
spark.conf.set only works in SQL
Executor memory can only be changed by AQE
questions.why: Session settings such as spark.sql.shuffle.partitions can change at run time, but executor and driver memory are set when the executors start, so they belong in the compute configuration. On serverless you cannot set them at all.

questions.q: In a Lakeflow Job, task C depends on tasks A and B. C should run as long as at least one of them succeeded. Which setting achieves this?
opts: Set C's "Run if dependencies" to At least one succeeded
Remove C's dependencies
Add retries to A and B
Schedule C one hour after A and B
questions.why: The Run if setting on a task controls how its dependencies' outcomes are combined: All succeeded is the default, and options include At least one succeeded, None failed and All done.

questions.q: A job's third task failed after the first two finished. After fixing the bug, what is the cheapest way to finish the run?
opts: Repair the run, which reruns only the failed task and the tasks after it
Start a brand-new run of the whole job
Delete the job and recreate it
Run each notebook by hand
questions.why: Repair run reruns failed tasks and the tasks that depend on them, reusing the successful tasks' results. A new full run would redo work that already succeeded.

questions.q: A job must run whenever new files land in a cloud storage location, not on a fixed schedule. Which trigger fits?
opts: A file arrival trigger
A cron schedule every minute
A continuous trigger on a SQL warehouse
Manual runs only
questions.why: File arrival triggers start a job when new files appear in the monitored location. Polling with a frequent cron schedule wastes runs when no data arrives.

questions.q: A gold job should run only after a silver table it reads has been updated by another team's pipeline, which finishes at unpredictable times. Which trigger is the best fit?
opts: A table update trigger on the silver table
A schedule at 6 am in the hope it is done
A file arrival trigger on the job's own notebook
A for each task
questions.why: Table update triggers start a job when the watched tables change, so the job runs when the data is actually ready. Data-driven triggers avoid both waiting too long and reading stale data.

questions.q: A job must run the same notebook for each of 30 country codes. Which task type avoids creating 30 separate tasks?
opts: A for each task that loops over the list of countries
An if/else condition task
A dashboard task
A file arrival trigger
questions.why: A for each task runs a nested task once per item in a list, passing the item as a parameter, with a configurable concurrency. Condition tasks branch; they don't loop.

questions.q: A job should send its data to a quarantine step only when a validation task reports errors. Which feature branches the workflow?
opts: An if/else condition task that checks a value such as a task value
Increasing the number of retries
A cron schedule
Cluster autoscaling
questions.why: An if/else condition task evaluates an expression, for example a task value set by the validation notebook, and runs the true or false branch accordingly.

questions.q: An API call in an ingestion task fails occasionally because of short network errors. What is the simplest fix in the job?
opts: Configure retries on that task, with a delay between attempts
Make every downstream task run if all done
Move the task to the end of the job
Disable the job's schedule
questions.why: Task-level retries rerun a failed task automatically, optionally with a wait between attempts, which handles transient failures without manual reruns.

questions.q: Which task types can a single Lakeflow Job orchestrate? (Choose two.)
opts: A Lakeflow Declarative Pipeline update
A SQL query or SQL file run on a SQL warehouse
A Git commit on someone's laptop
Restarting the workspace
questions.why: Lakeflow Jobs can run notebooks, Python scripts, SQL queries and files, dashboards, pipeline updates and more, with dependencies between them. They don't run actions on personal machines.

questions.q: Where do you work on a feature branch of a repository inside the Databricks workspace?
opts: A Git folder
A volume
The workspace's trash
A SQL warehouse
questions.why: Git folders connect a workspace folder to a remote Git repository so you can create branches, commit, push, pull and work toward pull requests from Databricks.

questions.q: In a bundle configuration, the catalog name differs between dev and prod. What is the recommended way to handle it?
opts: Define a variable and set different values per target
Keep two copies of every notebook
Edit the notebook by hand before each deployment
Hard-code prod and ask developers to be careful
questions.why: Bundles support variables with per-target overrides in the targets section of databricks.yml, so the same code deploys to dev, test and prod with environment-specific settings.

questions.q: Which CLI command checks a bundle's configuration for errors before anything is deployed?
opts: databricks bundle validate
databricks bundle destroy
databricks fs rm
databricks clusters delete
questions.why: bundle validate checks the configuration and reports problems without deploying. A typical CI pipeline runs validate, then deploy to a target, then run tests or the job.

questions.q: A CI pipeline should deploy a bundle's jobs and pipelines to production after a merge to main. Which command does the deployment?
opts: databricks bundle deploy -t prod
databricks bundle init
databricks workspace export
databricks jobs list
questions.why: bundle deploy -t prod deploys the bundle's resources using the prod target's settings. init creates a new bundle from a template, and the others don't deploy anything.

questions.q: Why do teams package jobs and pipelines as bundles rather than editing them in the UI in each workspace? (Choose two.)
opts: Definitions live in version control and can be reviewed in pull requests
The same definitions can be deployed repeatably to dev, test and prod
Bundles make jobs run without compute
Bundles remove the need for permissions
questions.why: Bundles describe resources as code, so changes are reviewed and versioned, and one definition deploys consistently to every environment. They don't change how jobs use compute or permissions.

questions.q: In the Spark UI, one stage has 200 tasks: most finish in 10 seconds but three take 15 minutes. What is the most likely cause?
opts: Data skew: a few keys hold far more rows than the rest
Too much driver memory
The cluster has too few users
Photon is enabled
questions.why: A large gap between median and maximum task time in one stage is the classic sign of skew. Fixes include adaptive query execution's skew join handling, salting hot keys, or filtering them separately.

questions.q: A stage shows large values for spill (disk). What does this mean?
opts: Tasks ran out of memory for their data and wrote it to disk, which slows them down
The job wrote its output to a volume
The cluster disk is full of logs
Delta deleted old files
questions.why: Spill means data didn't fit in execution memory and was written to disk and read back. More partitions (smaller tasks), less skew or more memory per core usually help.

questions.q: Which statements about liquid clustering are true? (Choose two.)
opts: You can change the clustering keys later without rewriting the existing data
It is defined with CLUSTER BY and replaces Hive-style partitioning and ZORDER for new tables
It requires partitioning the table by date first
It only works on external CSV tables
questions.why: Liquid clustering is set with CLUSTER BY, and keys can be changed with ALTER TABLE as query patterns change; existing data isn't rewritten immediately. It is the recommended layout for new Delta tables instead of partitioning plus ZORDER.

questions.q: What does predictive optimization do for Unity Catalog managed tables?
opts: Runs maintenance such as OPTIMIZE and VACUUM automatically when it would help
Predicts query results before they run
Moves tables to cheaper storage classes
Rewrites SQL queries to use fewer joins
questions.why: Predictive optimization decides when maintenance is worthwhile and runs operations like OPTIMIZE and VACUUM for managed tables, so teams don't need to schedule them by hand.

questions.q: A notebook calls df.collect() on a 300 GB DataFrame and the job fails with an out-of-memory error on the driver. What is the best fix?
opts: Write the result to a table, or aggregate before collecting, instead of collecting all rows to the driver
Add more worker nodes
Increase spark.sql.shuffle.partitions
Restart the cluster and try again
questions.why: collect brings every row to the driver, which can't hold 300 GB. More workers don't help the driver. Keep the work distributed and write results out, or collect only small aggregates.

questions.q: A Unity Catalog managed table is dropped. What happens to its data files?
opts: They are deleted, because Unity Catalog manages the table's storage
They stay in place and must be deleted by hand
They move to the user's home folder
Nothing; managed tables cannot be dropped
questions.why: For managed tables, Unity Catalog owns the storage, so DROP TABLE removes the data as well as the definition (after a short recovery window). Dropping an external table removes only the metadata.

questions.q: A team must keep data files in a storage path that other systems also read, and dropping the table must not delete them. Which table type fits?
opts: An external table
A managed table
A temporary view
A materialized view
questions.why: External tables point to data at a location you manage, registered through an external location. Dropping them removes only the table definition, leaving files for other systems.

questions.q: An analyst group has SELECT on main.sales.orders but gets a permission error when querying it. Which privileges are most likely missing?
opts: USE CATALOG on main and USE SCHEMA on main.sales
MODIFY on the table
CREATE TABLE on the schema
Workspace admin
questions.why: To read a table you need USE CATALOG on its catalog and USE SCHEMA on its schema, as well as SELECT on the table. Privileges granted on a catalog or schema are inherited by the objects inside it.

questions.q: Which statement grants the data_analysts group read access to every current and future table in the main.sales schema (given they can use the catalog)?
opts: GRANT USE SCHEMA, SELECT ON SCHEMA main.sales TO `data_analysts`
GRANT SELECT ON TABLE main.sales.* TO `data_analysts`
GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON METASTORE TO `data_analysts`
GRANT READ FILES ON SCHEMA main.sales TO `data_analysts`
questions.why: Granting SELECT on a schema is inherited by all tables in it, including ones created later, and USE SCHEMA lets the group reach them. Wildcards on table names are not supported, and granting on the metastore gives far too much.

questions.q: Sales reps should see only rows for their own region in a shared table, without separate copies per region. What does Unity Catalog provide for this?
opts: A row filter: a function applied to the table that returns which rows each user may see
A column mask on the region column
A separate external table per region
Revoking SELECT from everyone
questions.why: A row filter attaches a SQL function to a table and is evaluated for every query, often checking group membership with is_account_group_member. Column masks hide or transform values in a column instead of removing rows.

questions.q: Only the finance group should see full card numbers; everyone else should see only the last four digits. Which feature fits?
opts: A column mask function on the card number column
A row filter on the table
Dropping the column for everyone
A view per user
questions.why: A column mask is a function attached to a column that returns the real value or a masked one depending on who queries, for example the last four digits for users outside finance.

questions.q: A security team wants rules like "mask every column tagged pii for users outside the privacy group" applied across many tables from one place. Which Unity Catalog capability is designed for this?
opts: Attribute-based access control (ABAC) policies based on governed tags
Granting SELECT table by table
Copying tables into a restricted workspace
Turning off Unity Catalog for those tables
questions.why: ABAC policies use tags on data and conditions on users to apply row filters and column masks centrally, at the catalog or schema level, so new tagged tables are covered automatically instead of configuring each table.
